surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS was $1.21, below the preview’s $1.26–$1.27 quarterly consensus, despite rising about 19% year over year. Full-year EPS of $5.40 also came in below the preview’s roughly $5.45 projection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 diluted EPS rose approximately 19% to $1.21 from $1.02” and “full-year EPS increased 12% to $5.40 from $4.82.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | Q4 FY26 Consensus | $1.26–$1.27”; the full-year context says a $1.27 Q4 lands FY26 at “~$5.45 EPS.”

surprises.description: The RELEX forecasting and replenishment rollout slipped beyond the previously communicated Q2 FY27 target, and management gave no replacement completion date. The preview did not flag a risk of a further delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The RELEX forecasting and replenishment system implementation was delayed beyond the previously communicated Q2 fiscal 2027 target, with no new completion date provided due to process complexity across 13 countries.”

surprises.description: Q4 merchandise sales were stronger than the preview’s roughly $1.43 billion estimate, reaching nearly $1.5 billion. The reported growth included a substantial currency tailwind: constant-currency sales growth was 7.8%, while reported growth was 13.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net merchandise sales reached nearly $1.5 billion, up 13.8% year-over-year (7.8% in constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net merchandise sales | ~$1.43B (est.)”; the preview also said “Modest revenue upside is the single highest-confidence call.”

surprises.description: A $14.3 million combination of one-time and allocated costs weighed on Colombia’s operating margin. The preview anticipated Chile pre-opening costs, but did not flag this broader Colombia margin burden, including transfer-pricing reallocations and taxes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Colombia's operating margin was weighed down by roughly $14.3 million in one-time and allocated costs, including $4.2 million of Chile start-up expenses, $9 million in transfer pricing reallocations, and wealth and plastic taxes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Chile pre-opening builds from here into the spring 2027 launch,” but did not anticipate the $14.3 million Colombia cost burden.

surprises.description: The Q4 effective tax rate was much lower than the preview’s roughly 29% assumption, with discrete tax benefits providing an unanticipated boost. The favorable items were specific reversals and credits rather than an indicated ongoing tax-rate reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 effective tax rate fell to 25% from 32% due to roughly $2.5 million in discrete items including a $1.9 million U.S. tax contingency reversal and a $0.6 million Dominican Republic solar credit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “tax ~29%” and identified “Tax rate vs. ~29%” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Full-year SG&A rose to 13.2% of revenue from 12.9%, with technology spending and full-year CEO compensation adding to the margin pressure. The preview discussed SG&A and Chile pre-opening drag but did not identify these costs as drivers of the full-year increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year SG&A rose to 13.2% of revenue from 12.9%, with 20 basis points from technology investments and 10 basis points from full-year CEO compensation, pressuring operating margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “SG&A and pre-opening drag” and specified Q3 SG&A of 13.3%, but did not forecast the full-year 13.2% rate or cite technology and CEO costs.
